subject: Story AMSD-1820 completed
body: Story AMSD-1820 finished with status: completed

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-1820

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: Unsafe type assertion `(dispatch as { isReturn?: boolean }).isReturn` bypasses TypeScript's type system. The `MozioDispatch` type (derived from `dispatchSchema`) does not declare an `isReturn` property, so this cast is unverified at compile time. Under strict mode with `noImplicitAny` and `strictNullChecks`, this pattern is an unsafe escape hatch equivalent to untyped `any`. Furthermore, if `isReturn` is not actually present on the runtime object, the condition will always be `false`, meaning the entire return-trip discount splitting logic is dead code and acceptance criteria 1-4 are not met.
issues.suggestedFix: Add `isReturn` to the `MozioDispatch` type explicitly (e.g., `MozioDispatch = Omit<z.infer<typeof dispatchSchema>, 'report' | 'isReturn'> & { isReturn?: boolean; report: ... }`) or add it to the Zod `dispatchSchema`. Then access `dispatch.isReturn` directly without any cast. If the field comes from a different source, define a proper interface that extends `MozioDispatch` with the `isReturn` field.

issues.description: Acceptance criteria 3 and 4 are not satisfied. The implementation always splits the total discount evenly (50/50) across outbound and return legs. Criterion 3 requires that when a promo code is applied only to the return leg, only the return segment shows a discount (outbound shows none). Criterion 4 requires the converse for outbound-only. The even-split approach cannot distinguish which leg the promo applies to — it always populates both `outboundDiscount` and `returnDiscount` with non-zero values whenever any discount exists.
issues.suggestedFix: Track which leg each discount applies to (e.g., via a `leg` or `segment` field on the discount object from the dispatch report). Then assign the discount amount to `outboundDiscount` or `returnDiscount` accordingly, leaving the other undefined when the promo is leg-specific. If the upstream data does not currently carry leg information, that data model gap must be addressed before this fix can be considered complete.

issues.description: No vitest unit tests were added for the new return-trip discount splitting logic. The diff contains only source changes with no corresponding test files in test/unit/. All eight acceptance criteria require demonstrable verification, and criteria 1-8 specifically describe testable scenarios (return trip with promo, one-way regression, no-promo, negative-value prevention, per-leg targeting) that must have corresponding unit tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Add unit tests in `test/unit/services/submit-reservations/apply-report-discounts.service.spec.ts` (mirroring the src path) covering: (1) return trip with promo — both legs show discount, (2) sum of legs equals total, (3) promo on return only — return shows discount, outbound shows none, (4) promo on outbound only — outbound shows discount, return shows none, (5) no promo — neither leg shows discount, (6) one-way trip regression — discount matches promo value, (7) discount values never negative, (8) formatting consistency with other monetary values.

issues.description: The `MozioDispatchResponse` type is modified to add `activationTimestamp?: string` to the `Omit` list and re-add it as an optional field. This change is unrelated to the promo code discount fix described in AMSD-1820 and appears to be an out-of-scope modification that could introduce unintended type compatibility issues with existing consumers of `MozioDispatchResponse`.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the `activationTimestamp` change from this PR. If it is needed for a separate story, it should be submitted in its own PR with its own tests and acceptance criteria.

issues.description: The even-split approach (`segmentDiscount.amount.value / 2`) can produce floating-point precision issues for odd-cent amounts (e.g., $0.05 split into $0.025 per leg). While `getPreciseFloatNumber` is called, the return leg uses `segmentDiscount.amount.value - half` which may not exactly equal the original total due to rounding, potentially violating acceptance criterion 2 (sum of segment discounts equals total promo discount).
issues.suggestedFix: Use a rounding strategy that guarantees the two halves sum exactly to the total. For example, compute `half = getPreciseFloatNumber(Math.floor(total * 100 / 2) / 100)` and `otherHalf = getPreciseFloatNumber(total - half)`, or use integer-cent arithmetic throughout. Add a test case with an odd-cent discount amount to verify the sum is exact.

issues.description: The `sanitizeDiscount` helper function does not have an explicit return type annotation. While TypeScript can infer it, the project's strict compliance criteria require all function return types to be explicitly typed.
issues.suggestedFix: Add explicit return type: `function sanitizeDiscount(discount: SanitizedMozioDispatchDiscount | undefined): SanitizedMozioDispatchDiscount | undefined { ... }`

issues.description: The `segmentDiscount` local variable's type annotation uses `typeof currency` for the currency field type. While valid, this is an indirect type reference that could break if `currency`'s type changes. Prefer referencing the `Currency` type directly (as done in `mozio-order.ts`).
issues.suggestedFix: Import `Currency` from `~/types/models/money` and use it explicitly: `amount: { value: number; currency: Currency }`.
